questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been in Brisbane in my gap year and really liked the city and the weather, and then I wanted to study in an english speaking country. I chose University of Queensland because of the relatively high academic level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had the best half year in my life and would recommend everyone to go on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had an orientation week where I got a lot of practical information, and information about where to get help if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was the only one that found housing before I went to Brisbane. I was lucky to know someone who went to Brisbane the semester before so I could rent her room in a shared house.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living off campus because it is cheaper and a lot of the students that live on campus are very young. I was very lucky to find a very nice room in a house close o campus before I got to Brisbane, but the other students I talked to found housing when they arrived. It was generally hard for people to find housing in Brisbane, so be prepared to spend some money on hostels etc. the first weeks before finding housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the process very long. I had to complete a registration form and upload different documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a contact person from KU and a contact person from UQ. They both responded quite fast and they were a big help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I found the course registration very confusing because i did not find the UQ webpage with courses easy to navigate.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend contacting your contact person from UCPH and ask for a course list from UQ.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found the courses at UQ easier than the courses at UCPH, and I generally did not put in much effort to pass my courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses were held as seminars as at UCPH, but with less student participation than at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Principles of International Law 
Mediation and Conflict Management 
International Maritime Trade Law 
Fundamentals of the Common Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend the course International Maritime Trade Law. I had no expectations to the course, but I found it very interesting and the teacher of the course is really great. I would also recommend choosing intensive courses, because it gives a lot of sparetime and not much classes to attend. All of my courses were intensive courses which gave me the opportunity to plan my own days much more than if I had chosen normal courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend much more money on experiences and small trips than I had expected. I have been on so many great vacations and trips around Australia, which I would recommend to spend some money on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food at restaurants was less expensive than in Denmark. Alcohol was a lot more expensive in Australia than in Denmark. Other items generally cost the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is almost a club/society for everyone (political clubs, Harry Potter, surf, sports, etc.) The club QUEST is a club for exchange students that arrange weekly pub nights and some really nice weekend trips. I would recommend following them on facebook to get updated on their events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to as many pub nights and weekend trips with QUEST as possible. The surf club also arranges parties and trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going on roadtrips, for example Great Ocean Road or a roadtrip from Brisbane to Cairns. I would also recommend visiting Melbourne and Sydney. In Brisbane I can recommend the city beach at South Bank, shopping on Queen St., drinking a beer at Felons at sunset, hiking Mount Coot-Tha, visiting Lone Pine Koala Sanctuary and go for a walk in Roma Street Parklands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Australians are very laid back and easy-going.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to social events at campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The only big difference in the culture is the alcohol-policy. You cannot drink alcohol in most public places, so be aware of that.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The laid back culture and everyone being super nice and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Even though the whole process before going on exchange is very long it is all worth it when you arrive in Brisbane. 

Don't be nervous about the social aspect. Everyone are so friendly and just want to make new friends and experience as much as possible. There are plenty of events and parties where you can meet new friends. There are a lot of danish students in Brisbane which in my opinion is so nice because I have so many danish friends from my exchange that I can see after getting back home to Denmark. 

Don't stress about the academic aspect of the exchange. I honestly found the courses very easy and you will quickly get used to reading english texts.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If possible I would recommend finding housing before going to Brisbane, because a lot of people found it very hard to find housing when they arrived, and some stayed at hostels for a month. But everyone found housing in the end so please don't stress too much about it, but be prepared to spend some money on hostels in the first period of time.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friendships and all the great experiences (roadtrips, pub nights, weekend trips). Be prepared to not wanting to go back to Denmark after living in Australia. I could easily have stayed for another semester!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was the economical aspect of the exchange. Be prepared to spend a lot of money, but it is all worth it! I would recommend to start the whole scholarship process in good time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I was personally doubting whether an exchange was someting for me, but I can say that it honestly have been the greatest half year of my life, so I would recommend everyone to go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
